subject: Concord.ai trial validation checklist & success hypothesis
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn@concord.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Concord.ai trial validation checklist & success hypothesis

Evelyn — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed validation plan so we have alignment before we kick off the PoC:

Objective (what success looks like)
- Quality: end-user intent accuracy (top-1) >= 92% on your labeled held-out set; top-3 should be > 98%.
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 250ms for median payloads (~256 tokens); P95 <= 350ms for extended (512 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 80 requests/sec for the primary inference route during peak synthetic load.
- Cost: target marginal cost <= $0.0008 / token under the test traffic profile.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% for inference calls during ramp.

Proposed timeline & phases
1) Kickoff + access (days 0–3): credentials, sample dataset push, confirm metrics.
2) Smoke & baseline (week 1): functional validation, small-scale latency/quality runs.
3) Load ramp & stability (week 2): throughput tuning and autoscaling validation.
4) Quality evaluation (weeks 3–4): run labeled evaluation suite, compute KPIs, and review.

Owners (Redwood / Concord)
- Program lead: Marcus Lin (Redwood) — overall coordination and SOW.
- Test ops: Monica Patel (Redwood) — sandbox instantiation, load scripts, monitoring hooks.
- Evaluation & metrics: Lauren Bishop (Redwood) — rubric, acceptance checks, report.
- Data & security: Concord security lead (you to introduce) — dataset access and privacy needs.

Deliverables attached: concord-trial-outline.pdf, measurement-template.xlsx (measurement template + sample scripts).

Immediate asks / next steps
- Confirm acceptance of the success hypothesis above (esp. latency/quality targets).
- Share security contact + procurement contact for SOW routing.
- Approve the attached outline so we can push a SOW draft and schedule a kickoff (I can be flexible as early as next Tue).

Thanks again — I’ll start drafting SOW v2 with the test phases and roles.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. High level, Concord likes the structure. A few notes from our side before we lock the SOW: 

- Latency: our product team asks if we can tighten the P95 target to 200ms for the 256-token median payload (we understand extended 512-token targets can be relaxed). Is that feasible with your suggested configuration?
- Privacy/addendum: our legal team requires a data processing addendum for any sample data ingestion. I’ll loop in procurement (procure@concord.ai) formally.
- Procurement: please route the SOW to procure@concord.ai. Our PO process typically needs a 30-day review.

Also, please ensure the measurement-template.xlsx includes the exact eval script commands and the expected CSV schema so our engineering team can run the runs in parallel.

Best,
Evelyn Shaw
Head of Product — Concord.ai

Evelyn — thanks, and understood on procurement and DPA. Quick responses and an updated plan below.

1) Latency target: we can move the baseline P95 for 256-token median payload down to 200ms but will make that a gated target in the SOW:
   - Gate A (smoke): P95 <= 250ms across smoke tests (week 1).
   - Gate B (performance acceptance): P95 <= 200ms for 256 tokens during a calibrated 1-hour soak at expected request mix (week 2).

2) Privacy / DPA: noted. I’ll include a DPA attachment in SOW v2 and route to procurement. Please confirm procurement contact below so I can add them to the DocuSign flow.

3) Measurement template: attached updated measurement-template.xlsx includes the run commands, expected CSV schema (id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, model_prob, expected_label), and an example script to compute top-1/top-3 accuracy.

Proposed phased test schedule (concrete)
- Week 0 (0–3 days): credentials + sample push + send SOW v2 (Marcus).
- Week 1 (smoke): functional checks, baseline latency numbers, and confirm monitoring hooks (Monica).
- Week 2 (ramp): throughput validation and performance acceptance run (Monica + infra).
- Weeks 3–4 (evaluation): full labeled runs and quality report (Lauren).

Owners (updated)
- Program lead: Marcus Lin (marcus_lin@redwood.ai) — SOW, executive sync, liaison.
- Test ops & infra: Monica Patel (monica_patel@redwood.ai) — sandbox, load scripts, Cloud infra touchpoints.
- Evaluation & metrics: Lauren Bishop (lauren_bishop@redwood.ai) — evaluation rubric, scripts, reporting.

I’ve attached SOW draft (sow-draft-concord-v2.pdf) with the gating language above and added a checkbox for DPA acceptance. If that looks good I’ll start the DocuSign flow and copy procurement. Proposed kickoff: Tue 2027-05-25 at 09:00 PT — does that work?

—
Marcus Lin

I’ll prepare SOW v2 and start the DocuSign flow after we confirm procurement contact.
